\[
a_1 + a_2 + a_3 + \cdots + a_n = 12 \quad \text{and} \quad a_1 \circ a_2 \circ a_3 \circ \cdots \circ a_n = 0
\]
where the operations are performed from left to right; that is, $a_1 \circ a_2 \circ a_3$ means $(a_1 \circ a_2) \circ a_3.$

Let \(F_s(x)\) be the number of sequences with total sum \(s\) and current value \(x\) after left-to-right evaluation.

We start with
\[
F_0(0)=1.
\]
If the current value is \(x\) and we append a positive integer \(k\), then
\[
x\circ k=
\begin{cases}
x-k,& x\text{ odd and }k\text{ even},\\
x+k,& \text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\]

Using dynamic programming up to sum \(12\), the relevant negative states before the final term are:

\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c|c}
s & k=12-s & x=-k & F_s(x)\\
\hline
7 & 5 & -5 & 4\\
8 & 4 & -4 & 4\\
9 & 3 & -3 & 20\\
10 & 2 & -2 & 28\\
11 & 1 & -1 & 101
\end{array}
\]

To finish at \(0\), the previous current value must be \(-k\), so appending \(k=12-s\) gives
\[
(-k)+k=0.
\]
Subtraction can never produce \(0\) because it requires an odd current value minus an even number, which is odd.

Thus the number of valid sequences is
\[
4+4+20+28+101=157.
\]
